courseReview.name: Personal & Professional Development
courseReview.contribution: Mandatory Year-1 development.

courseReview.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
courseReview.contribution: Direct accounting contribution: accepted accounting theory and practice, corporate annual reports and financial-statement analysis support organisational decisions. The title alone does not establish the whole external corporate-finance syllabus.

courseReview.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
courseReview.contribution: examines managerial, organisational and societal implications of AI and technological change

courseReview.name: Transnational Business Law
courseReview.contribution: covers legal frameworks for contracts, trade, company activity and digital commerce across borders

courseReview.name: Money, Banking & Finance
courseReview.contribution: Direct financial decision-making: cases develop analysis of financial data, risk, investment, budgeting and business value. This is partial corporate-finance correspondence, not identical external coverage.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Economics
courseReview.contribution: provides economic foundations on firms, markets, incentives and macroeconomic conditions

courseReview.name: International Macroeconomics
courseReview.contribution: examines growth, inflation, business cycles and policy shaping the international business environment

courseReview.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
courseReview.contribution: develops microeconomic and behavioural analysis of consumer and firm decisions

courseReview.name: Public Economics
courseReview.contribution: examines market failure, externalities, taxation and public intervention affecting firms

courseReview.name: Econometrics
courseReview.contribution: provides econometric tools for causal and predictive analysis of business data

courseReview.name: Consumer Product Design
courseReview.contribution: develops product innovation through customer needs, design, costing and team development

courseReview.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
courseReview.contribution: examines marketing strategy, consumer psychology and responsible customer engagement

courseReview.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
courseReview.contribution: develops business strategy from vision to execution and responsible digital transformation

courseReview.name: Market Research
courseReview.contribution: Direct applied empirical business research: students plan and conduct real market research, analyse results and formulate business recommendations. This course-based project does not reproduce a separate 12-EC bachelor thesis.

courseReview.name: International Business & Governance
courseReview.contribution: examines institutions, culture, governance and corporate responsibility in global business

courseReview.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
courseReview.contribution: provides business foundations while developing venture creation, business models and market validation

courseReview.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courseReview.contribution: provides research design, surveys, experiments and statistical analysis for management questions

courseReview.name: Personal Leadership
courseReview.contribution: develops leadership theory, self-awareness and applied leadership practice

courseReview.name: Leadership Communication
courseReview.contribution: develops leadership communication, ethical influence and persuasive practice

courseReview.name: Leadership & Diversity Management
courseReview.contribution: examines inclusive leadership and diversity management in organisations

courseReview.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
courseReview.contribution: examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structures through organisational psychology

courseReview.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
courseReview.contribution: Direct business negotiation and influence: persuasive arguments, language, negotiation processes and interest-based strategic interaction. This is not a general corporate-strategy counterpart.

courseReview.name: AI Ethics
courseReview.contribution: examines ethical and societal questions raised by artificial intelligence

courseReview.name: Database Management Systems
courseReview.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides relational database and SQL skills for structured data. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courseReview.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
courseReview.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: develops algorithmic problem-solving and data structures for computational applications. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Data Science
courseReview.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: develops data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation across disciplinary datasets. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courseReview.name: Machine Learning
courseReview.contribution: introduces machine-learning models for prediction and analysis of real datasets

courseReview.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
courseReview.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: develops neural-network and deep-learning methods for advanced AI applications. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Programming
courseReview.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides programming foundations in Python. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courseReview.name: Mathematical Methods
courseReview.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides mathematical foundations for quantitative modelling. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courseReview.name: Linear Algebra
courseReview.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides linear-algebra foundations for quantitative and machine-learning models. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courseReview.name: Probability & Statistics
courseReview.contribution: Complementary analytical tools: provides probability, statistical inference and simulation foundations for risk and analytics. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

courseReview.name: R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation
courseReview.contribution: Environmental science/technical or sector-specific content has insufficient business-management weight here; replaced by stronger business or empirical-method content.

courseReview.name: Governance of Sustainability
courseReview.contribution: Complementary regulatory and societal context: governmental and nongovernmental actors, interests, public opinion and policy enforcement explain sustainability governance. This is not a dedicated responsible-organisation course.

courseReview.name: Sustainable Farming & Innovation
courseReview.contribution: Environmental science/technical or sector-specific content has insufficient business-management weight here; replaced by stronger business or empirical-method content.

courseReview.name: Sustainability Essentials I
courseReview.contribution: Complementary environmental framework: planetary boundaries identify environmental limits relevant to responsible products and business strategy; this is not business management training.

courseReview.name: Sustainability Essentials II
courseReview.contribution: Environmental science/technical or sector-specific content has insufficient business-management weight here; replaced by stronger business or empirical-method content.

courseReview.name: Climate Change
courseReview.contribution: Complementary climate context: anthropogenic drivers, environmental and societal impacts, adaptation, mitigation, climate governance and justice inform sustainable business risk and responsibility.

courseReview.name: Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy
courseReview.contribution: Direct sustainable product and process analysis: life-cycle environmental evaluation and strategic circular-economy planning support responsible enterprise decisions.

courseReview.name: Renewable System Design
courseReview.contribution: Environmental science/technical or sector-specific content has insufficient business-management weight here; replaced by stronger business or empirical-method content.

courseReview.name: Ethics
courseReview.contribution: Complementary normative reasoning: virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, responsibility, equality, wealth, future generations and climate support ethical business judgments. No dedicated business-ethics case syllabus is claimed.

courseReview.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courseReview.contribution: Complementary empirical method: qualitative question design, interpretation, small-team projects and reflexivity about complexity and power support organisational inquiry; business topics are not guaranteed.

courseReview.name: Social Psychology
courseReview.contribution: Complementary behavioural foundations: scientific social psychology examines how others influence thought, feelings and behaviour; its organisational or customer application is specific supporting work.

courseReview.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
courseReview.contribution: Complementary academic and professional communication: rhetorical analysis, argument, academic writing and oral presentation support communicating organisational research. Historical and contemporary rhetoric is not an empirical business-research course.

academicReview.comparability: Three provisional, evidence-backed concepts remain: broad business administration; business analytics and digital transformation; responsible entrepreneurship and sustainable strategy. Each contains sustained actual business study; a coherent adjacent STEM degree would not suffice under the CP119 distinction. Four environmental science/technology placements in the third route are replaced with directly useful business and research content. Pairwise differences are [{'pair': [1, 2], 'differentCourses': 10}, {'pair': [1, 3], 'differentCourses': 6}, {'pair': [2, 3], 'differentCourses': 12}]. Three is the maximum, not a target. Final comparative approval is withheld because current official thesis-entry sources conflict.
